subject: Whistic onboarding — scoped retention & upload cadence questions
messages:
From: Claire Bowers <claire@clearspanhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Whistic onboarding — scoped retention & upload cadence questions

Hi Irene —

Thanks for picking this up. We're starting the Whistic profile onboarding for ClearSpan Health and have a couple of constraints we need to confirm before we push an initial evidence bundle:

- Can Redwood accept an ephemeral upload window (S3 presigned objects with TTL) for temporally sensitive proofs (logs, certs)? Our security ops team prefers 7-day TTLs for staging.
- What's the minimum retention Redwood expects for uploaded evidence on vendor portals vs. our own retention policy (we'd prefer to expire staging uploads after 30 days unless flagged).
- Do you have a preferred manifest format? I attached a simple inventory (clearspan_evidence_manifest.xlsx) that maps CAIQ sections to file types.

If this flow needs an API token/proxy account on Whistic we can provision one; please confirm scope and low-privilege recommendations.

We'd like to get a minimal proof bundle into the portal by Sep 10 if possible.

Thanks —
Claire
Claire Bowers
Head of Security Programs
ClearSpan Health
attachments: clearspan_evidence_manifest.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Claire Bowers <claire@clearspanhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Whistic onboarding — scoped retention & upload cadence questions

Hi Claire —

Appreciate the manifest — that helps. Short answers up front, then a recommended path: 

1) Ephemeral uploads: yes — we support presigned S3 uploads for staged proof artifacts. 7-day TTL for staging is acceptable as long as:
   - You maintain a canonical copy (we recommend your retention policy keep a copy for 90 days).
   - Any evidence that will be referenced in future audits is marked as "persist" in the manifest so we can ingest a durable copy into our evidence store.

2) Minimum retention expectations:
   - For portal-hosted artifacts we ask customers to signal which files are "audit-grade" (recommended retention 1+ year) vs ephemeral (30 days).
   - If ClearSpan needs to keep everything for regulatory reasons, we can set a longer ingest TTL on a per-file basis during upload.

3) Manifest format: your XLSX is fine. For automation we prefer a CSV with columns: file_name, caiq_section, evidence_type, presign_ttl_days, persist_flag. If you can convert, that will make automated ingestion faster.

Next steps I propose:
- Quick 20-min call to confirm persist flags and token scope (Jonas can join for the API details).
- You provision a low-privilege portal account or API key for presign creation and share it over the secure link we provide.
- We'll run a dry run upload into your Whistic profile and surface any CAIQ mapping mismatches.

Would Sep 4 10:00am PT or Sep 4 2:00pm PT work for you?

Best,
Irene Choi
Manager, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
From: Claire Bowers <claire@clearspanhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Whistic onboarding — scoped retention & upload cadence questions

Irene —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Sep 4 windows don't work for our compliance lead; can we do Sep 6 11:00am PT instead? Jonas joining is perfect.

Per your notes:
- I've converted the manifest into CSV and included a sample row that marks two log files as ephemeral and one SOC2 artifact as persist. See attached: clearspan_evidence_manifest.csv (exported from your spreadsheet).
- We're happy to keep canonical copies for 90 days and mark audit-grade files for longer retention.
- For the API token: we can create a token scoped to presign:create and profile:upload (no profile:admin). Would that be sufficient?

Attachments included:
- clearspan_evidence_manifest.csv (csv)
- sample-s3-presign-policy.txt (txt)

Can you confirm whether Redwood needs additional metadata (SHA256, upload timestamp) to validate ingest, or if the presign signature and manifest row are sufficient?

Claire
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Bowers <claire@clearspanhealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Whistic onboarding — scoped retention & upload cadence questions

Claire —

Thanks, this looks good. Quick confirmations from our side and one pragmatic ask: 

- Token scope you proposed (presign:create + profile:upload) is exactly what we recommend for minimal privileges. Please limit IP ranges where possible.
- Metadata: please add SHA256 and a presign_ttl_days column in the manifest. That makes automated verification simpler and avoids re-hashing on our side during ingest.
- Timeline: we'll do a dry-run ingestion during the Sep 6 call. After dry-run success we'll transition two artifacts to "persist" and take an internal snapshot for audit.

Action items (owners):
- Claire: share the portal token (secure link) and upload the CSV manifest by Sep 6 09:00 PT.
- Jonas: I'll hand the presign runbook and small checklist to you for the call (presign_runbook_v0.3.pdf).
- Irene: run the dry-run ingestion and report any CAIQ mapping gaps back to Claire within 24 hours.

If that all looks correct I'll mark this ready and add the Sep 6 call to calendars.

Ben Carter
Security TPM, Redwood Inference
